## Using Vector Stores

As discussed in [indexing](/python/framework/module_guides/indexing), one of the most common types of Index is the VectorStoreIndex. The API calls to create the [embeddings](/python/framework/module_guides/indexing#what-is-an-embedding) in a VectorStoreIndex can be expensive in terms of time and money, so you will want to store them to avoid having to constantly re-index things.

LlamaIndex supports a [huge number of vector stores](/python/framework/module_guides/storing/vector_stores) which vary in architecture, complexity and cost. In this example we'll be using Chroma, an open-source vector store.

First you will need to install chroma:

```
pip install chromadb
```

title: pgvector
heading_path: pgvector > Frequently Asked Questions > Can I store vectors with more precision?
text:
#### Can I store vectors with more precision?

You can use the `double precision[]` or `numeric[]` type to store vectors with more precision.

```sql
CREATE TABLE items (id bigserial PRIMARY KEY, embedding double precision[]);

-- use {} instead of [] for Postgres arrays
INSERT INTO items (embedding) VALUES ('{1,2,3}'), ('{4,5,6}');
```

Optionally, add a [check constraint](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html) to ensure data can be converted to the `vector` type and has the expected dimensions.

```sql
ALTER TABLE items ADD CHECK (vector_dims(embedding::vector) = 3);
```

Use [expression indexing](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-expressional.html) to index (at a lower precision):

```sql
CREATE INDEX ON items USING hnsw ((embedding::vector(3)) vector_l2_ops);
```

### Other Model Types

IBM watsonx.ai also offers:

- **Deploy on Demand Models** - Curated models that require creating a dedicated deployment first
- **Embedding Models** - For generating text embeddings (e.g., `ibm/granite-embedding-278m-multilingual`)
- **Reranker Models** - For improving search results (e.g., `cross-encoder/ms-marco-minilm-l-12-v2`)
- **Vision and Guardrail Models** - Models with APIs or payloads that differ from the provider's current text/chat workflow

:::info Additional Model Types Not Currently Supported

The promptfoo WatsonX provider focuses on **text generation and chat models only**. Deploy on Demand, embedding, and reranker models use different API endpoints and workflows. For these model types, use IBM's API directly or create a [custom provider](/docs/providers/custom-api/).

### Vector Store Integrations and Storage

Most of our vector store integrations store the entire index (vectors + text) in the vector store itself. This comes with the major benefit of not having to explicitly persist the index as shown above, since the vector store is already hosted and persisting the data in our index.

The vector stores that support this practice are:

- AzureAISearchVectorStore
- ChatGPTRetrievalPluginClient
- CassandraVectorStore
- ChromaVectorStore

### Vector Type

Each vector takes `4 * dimensions + 8` bytes of storage. Each element is a single-precision floating-point number (like the `real` type in Postgres), and all elements must be finite (no `NaN`, `Infinity` or `-Infinity`). Vectors can have up to 16,000 dimensions.

## How Native ADK Tracing Fits Promptfoo

ADK 2.x emits OpenTelemetry spans such as:

- `invocation` (legacy ADK) or `invoke_workflow <name>` (ADK 2.13 v2)
- `invoke_agent weather_agent`
- `generate_content <model>`
- `execute_tool get_weather`

The example provider preserves Promptfoo's W3C `traceparent`, starts a small provider span beneath it, and exports ADK's child spans to Promptfoo's built-in OTLP receiver. On ADK 2.9.2 and 2.12, look for tool arguments in `gcp.vertex.agent.tool_call_args`. ADK 2.13’s v2 schema uses `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and drops `call_llm`. Use `generate_content <model>` to count model calls across these releases.
